turns.answer_text:
# Analysis

**Top Tc samples in the data:**

| Composition | Tc (K) |
|---|---|
| H2S | 185 (H, S not design variables — excluded) |
| Hg1Ba2Ca2Cu3O8 | 132 (Hg not a design variable) |
| Ba2Ca2Cu3O | 126 (likely a (Cu,C)-based analogue, ill-defined O) |
| Tl0.5Pb0.5... | 117–120 (Tl not a variable) |
| **Bi1.4Pb0.5Sb0.1Sr2Ca2Cu3O** | **109** |
| Bi2Sr2Ca1Cu2O10 | 110 |
| Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O | 105.7 |

**Key insight:** All records >100 K are cuprates with the layered structure (charge-reservoir block)–(Sr/Ba)–(Ca–CuO₂ multilayer). With the available variables (no Hg, Tl), the best accessible family is the **Pb-doped Bi-2223 cuprate** (Bi,Pb)₂Sr₂Ca₂Cu₃O₁₀, which appears at 105–110 K in the data.

**Robustness considerations:**
- Bi-2223 is famously tolerant to stoichiometric variation: data shows Bi₂Sr₂Ca₂Cu₃O at 105.7 K and Bi₁.₄Pb₀.₅Sb₀.₁Sr₂Ca₂Cu₃O at 109 K — ±20–30% cation changes shift Tc only a few K. This is a broad optimum, not a sharp peak.
- Pb substitution for Bi (~20%) stabilizes the 2223 phase and slightly raises Tc — I include it.
- Oxygen content near optimal doping (O₁₀ for 2223) sits on a plateau of the Tc-vs-doping dome; ±5% in O fraction stays on the plateau (contrast with sharply doping-sensitive La₂₋ₓSrₓCuO₄ around x=0.15).

**Chosen stoichiometry:** Bi₁.₆Pb₀.₄Sr₂Ca₂Cu₃O₁₀ (total atoms = 19)

- Bi = 1.6/19 = 0.084211
- Pb = 0.4/19 = 0.021053
- Sr = 2/19 = 0.105263
- Ca = 2/19 = 0.105263
- Cu = 3/19 = 0.157895
- O = 10/19 = 0.526316

All within observed ranges (O ≤ 0.6977, Cu ≤ 0.4545, Sr ≤ 0.2857, Ca ≤ 0.2727, Bi ≤ 0.5220, Pb ≤ 0.5). All other elements set to 0 — mixing in Fe/As (pnictide chemistry, Tc ≤ 45 K) or Nb/V/B (conventional, Tc ≤ 40 K) would only dilute the cuprate phase. Expected Tc ≈ 108–110 K, robust to ±5% perturbation of any single fraction.

**Final: O=0.526316, Cu=0.157895, Ba=0, Sr=0.105263, Y=0, Ca=0.105263, La=0, Bi=0.084211, Fe=0, Nb=0, C=0, Pr=0, As=0, B=0, Pb=0.021053, Ce=0, Mo=0, V=0, Zn=0, Ni=0**
